archetype.name: Title Contender (slow start)
archetype.definition: Last year's best team on the site, 62-20 with 13 playoff wins, with three games of 2026-27 showing a break-even team that has not yet looked like itself on offense.

report.headline: A 62-win team playing like a .500 one, mostly through noise
report.take:
San Antonio arrives as the defending top dog. Last season it went 62-20, ranked first on the site, finished top four in both offensive and defensive rating and won 13 playoff games. Three games into this one it is 1-2, 19th on the site, with a Net Rtg of exactly 0 and 336 points scored and allowed. Its two losses came at home to OKC and HOU, the second by four. Then it handled Dallas on the road, 122-106. That is a modest start against a demanding opening slate, not a crisis.

The offense is the real dip. ORtg sits at 109.9, 17th and below the league's 112.4, after last year's 119.6. The cause is plain: Victor Wembanyama is using 30.7% of possessions at a 47.6 TS %, and the team's FT Rate of 23.5 ranks 26th. The guards are carrying the shot-making. De'Aaron Fox is at a 69.1 TS % with 25 assists and a 6.9 BPM, and Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle have added 60 and 58 points. Fox at that efficiency won't last, but Wembanyama at that efficiency won't either, and the second correction is the bigger one.

The defense looks worse than it is. Opponents are hitting 41.7% from three, 28th, a gap of 7.7 points over the league. Three games of opponent shooting is close to pure variance, and the things a defense controls look healthy. San Antonio ranks 3rd in DRB % at 78.3 and 9th in Opp Rim Rate. Its own ball security is strong, 4th in TOV %. Strip out the three-point luck and this defense is close to last year's top-three unit.

The structural issue is the frontcourt behind Wembanyama, which grades a D. The team is 44.8 points better per 100 with him on the floor. Luke Kornet, Carter Bryant and Harrison Barnes all carry deeply negative On-Off numbers, Bryant's at -64. The minutes when Wembanyama sits are where San Antonio is losing games, and fixing them matters more than any shooting slump.

strengths.title: Fox and the guard depth
strengths.body: The backcourt grades B+ and is doing most of the scoring while Wembanyama finds his touch. Fox has been the engine, efficient and setting teammates up, and Harper and Castle give the offense two more ball-handlers who can create. Fox's 69.1 TS % will cool, but the group's depth is real.

strengths.title: Finishing possessions on the glass
strengths.body: San Antonio is ending opponents' trips with a DRB % of 78.3, third in the league, and keeping teams away from the rim. That is the same profile as last year's 77.3 DRB % and is driven by Wembanyama's size, so it should hold.

strengths.title: Protecting the ball
strengths.body: A TOV % of 11.7 ranks fourth, in line with last season's 11.8. With three primary handlers in the backcourt, this looks like a durable trait rather than a hot start.

concerns.title: Minutes without Wembanyama
concerns.body: The frontcourt grades a D because the bigs behind Wembanyama are getting run over. Kornet's On-Off is -51.2, and Bryant and Barnes are even further below or close behind him. Wembanyama's +44.8 shows the gap. This is a rotation problem that won't fix itself the way shooting luck does.

concerns.title: Wembanyama's inefficient volume
concerns.body: He leads the team in usage at 30.7% but sits at a 47.6 TS %. Paired with a FT Rate that ranks 26th, the offense is settling for too many tough jumpers. Expect his efficiency to climb toward his norm, which is the single biggest lever for the offense.

concerns.title: Opponents' hot three-point shooting
concerns.body: Opponents are making 41.7% of their threes, 7.7 points above the league. That has erased an otherwise solid defense in the early numbers. Three games of this mostly reflects variance rather than scheme, but it has already cost a close loss to Houston.

trend.note: Two losses to open, then a 16-point road win at Dallas. The scoring margin is level, and the luck stat is a single close loss.

weekAhead.headline: Three soft defenses, then a test against first-ranked Minnesota
weekAhead.body:
Three of the four games come against defenses near the bottom of the league. Sacramento is 0-3, 29th on the site, with a 122.5 DRtg. Utah, seen twice, has the 28th-ranked defense at 123.0. This is exactly the week for San Antonio's half-court offense to shake off the slow start, and three of the four are at home. The Kings in particular have been giving centers far more than their usual output, an obvious opening for Wembanyama.

The Halloween home game against Minnesota is the measuring stick. The Wolves are 3-0 and first on the site, with the league's best DRtg at 96.2 and its best 3P % at 42.4. Against a hot-shooting team, the Spurs' defensive three-point luck will be tested. A 3-1 week is the reasonable target, and the Minnesota result is the one that says most about where this team stands.

keyMatchups.title: Wembanyama against Sacramento's interior
keyMatchups.body: The Kings have allowed centers well above their usual production, with a points-rebounds-assists gap ranking 29th. It's a good spot for Wembanyama to get easy looks and lift his TS %.

keyMatchups.title: Spurs guards against Utah's backcourt defense
keyMatchups.body: Utah has allowed big scoring games to shooting guards while holding centers below their averages. That points the offense toward Harper, Fox and Castle in both Jazz games rather than forcing it inside.

keyMatchups.title: Minnesota's shooting against the perimeter defense
keyMatchups.body: The Wolves lead the league in 3P % and in REB %. San Antonio's defensive rebounding is a real counter, but its perimeter defense has been leaking threes.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Wembanyama's efficiency rebounds against Sacramento and Utah, and how the minutes without him hold up against Minnesota.

restOfSeason.body:
Three games don't overturn a 62-win, top-ranked season. The weak spots so far are mostly things that regress: opponents' three-point shooting and Wembanyama's TS %. The traits that carried last year are intact: defensive rebounding, keeping opponents away from the rim and taking care of the ball. The 27-win pace the site shows is an artifact of the sample. Expect the offense to climb back toward the top ten and the Net Rtg to settle well above zero, which puts San Antonio in the 50-58 win range.

What keeps the projection below last year's 62 is the bench frontcourt. If those minutes keep bleeding at this rate, the Spurs will be a very good team with a fragile second unit rather than a dominant one. Houston's 3-0 start also means the division won't be handed to them.

confidence.note: Three games, two against strong opponents.
